transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Tue Jun 9, 2026 15:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Evan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Fernridge Head of Product), Tom Becker (Platform Eng), Neha Patel (Security)

[00:00] Evan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really appreciate you carving out time today. I'm Evan, AE on the account, with Maya and Diego from our onboarding and solutions team.
[00:15] Sofia Alvarez: Hi, thanks, Evan. We—yeah excited to get started, I'll try to keep the background context short, but quick intro: Fernridge is piloting ML-driven product descriptions across our marketplace, main goal is latency under 150ms p50 for interactive edits and privacy of merchant data.
[00:30] Diego Ramos: Got it, thanks. Quick clarifying Q — when you say "interactive edits" is that end-user on storefront or internal content team?
[00:40] Sofia Alvarez: Mostly internal content ops to start, but we want to be voice-ready later so latency matters.
[00:48] Tom Becker: Our infra team will host the staging environment in AWS us-west-2, VPC controls are strict—egress only to allowlist, and we have a central firewall team.
[00:58] Maya Chen: Perfect, that aligns with the Dedicated vs Private convo we usually have. Today we'll capture runbook inputs and walk through the first 30 days.

[05:12] Evan Park: I'll run through the activation playbook high level — kickoff, env access, baseline benchmarks, pilot data ingestion, then iterate. The typical milestones: day 0-7 access and config, week 2 run benchmarks, week 3 begin QA with content ops.
[05:40] Sofia Alvarez: That schedule looks ok. One ask — we need clarity on audit logs and retention, our legal team requires 1 year retention and proof of access logs.
[05:53] Neha Patel: And for encryption: are client-side keys supported or do you require Redwood KMS? We have to keep merchant PII in our own key domain.
[06:08] Diego Ramos: We support customer-managed keys in Private deployments and can integrate with KMS for Dedicated in certain arrangements. For the hosted API we use Redwood-managed keys; we can produce audit logs with request IDs and token-level traces.
[06:26] Neha Patel: Okay can you share the SOC2 scope doc and an example audit log within the next few days?
[06:35] Evan Park: Yes, we'll attach our compliance pack. I'll note that as an action.

[12:02] Tom Becker: Network-wise we will need the egress IPs or allowlist ranges. Who on your side points us to the correct list?
[12:10] Diego Ramos: For hosted you'll get a small set of ranges; for Dedicated/private it depends on deployment. I'll follow up with a short matrix mapping deployment -> required network artifacts.
[12:25] Tom Becker: Cool. Also about kb cache — sorry, cacheing — we have variable sequence lengths, do you have suggestions for batching to keep latency predictable?
[12:36] Diego Ramos: Yes — we usually recommend continuous batching with an SLO-aware limiter in the runtime. For content ops use-case where bursts happen during ingest windows, enable prefix caching and tune max-batch-size to keep p50 low. We'll provide recommended initial values in the benchmark script.

[18:00] Sofia Alvarez: Can we talk about success metrics? For us it's accuracy (coherence with product fields), latency, and cost per 1000 requests. We'll send a small labeled set for evaluation.
[18:14] Maya Chen: Great — please attach the labeled set to the ticket, SE will run evals and we'll surface regressions. We'll also add quality monitors into the console and threshold alerts.

[24:45] Evan Park: Logistics: we recommend a 2-week staging window. Diego will run a dry benchmark with synthetic payloads, then we'll swap in your real but obfuscated sample dataset. Can you commit to supplying a 500-item sample by Thursday?
[24:58] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, we can do 500 items — we'll obfuscate merchant names and any PII.

[30:05] Neha Patel: A question on data residency — some merchants require EU data residency. Do you offer regional hosting for production?
[30:15] Evan Park: Yes, Redwood supports region-specific deployments for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we have EU regions and options; we'll capture the production residency requirements in the runbook.

[36:20] Tom Becker: API keys and service accounts—what's the workflow to create service accounts for staging? Need least privilege.
[36:30] Diego Ramos: We'll provide a service account template and IAM role recommendations. For private deployments you can also map to your own service principal.

[41:50] Sofia Alvarez: Can you also explain rollback and fallback behavior if a model update causes a quality regression? We need an emergency rollback path.
[42:00] Maya Chen: Yes — our rollout policy in the console allows canary rollouts with automatic health checks. If quality drops past a threshold we auto-fallback to a pinned model. We'll document thresholds and manual override steps.

[47:10] Evan Park: Looping back to procurement — do you have an NDA in place? It'll help Neha feel comfortable while sharing deeper logs.
[47:20] Neha Patel: We have a standard vendor NDA but prefer to review your security questionnaire too.
[47:30] Evan Park: I'll share both the NDA and our security questionnaire.

[50:05] Diego Ramos: Quick note — for the benchmark we'll need a mix of short and long prompts to mirror your real distribution; Tom we'll ping you for sample payload shapes.
[50:15] Tom Becker: OK will do.

[52:40] Maya Chen: Recap: actions are Evan to send runbook and compliance docs, Diego to prepare benchmark/script, Tom to share network and sample payloads, Neha to confirm compliance scope, Sofia to provide labeled evaluation set. We'll schedule the environment access walkthrough for next Thursday.
[52:58] Sofia Alvarez: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[53:10] Evan Park: Appreciate it, we'll follow up with the artifacts and the calendar invite. Bye all.

End of transcript.
questions: Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/private?
What are the network allowlist requirements for hosted vs dedicated?
How are audit logs surfaced and what retention options exist?
